original_record.question: Carl tries to divide the large shape of squares into smaller pieces using only copies of the T-piece and the F-piece shown on the right. (Pieces may be turned over or around.) What is the smallest possible number of the T-pieces that he can achieve? <image1>
original_record.solution: F-pieces are made up from 4 small squares and Tpieces from 3. So 22 squares could be covered either by $4 \mathrm{Fs}$ and 2 Ts or by $1 \mathrm{~F}$ and 6 Ts. These diagrams show how Carl might have done it both ways, but the smallest number of T-pieces is 2 . ![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/2023_12_27_0f4ed2787981bb911326g-011.jpg?height=228&width=462&top_left_y=300&top_left_x=1316)
